title: QBR action plan template for model quality regression
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document is a repeatable QBR action-plan template to triage, contain, and communicate model quality regressions observed for enterprise customers. It is intended for Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, and the Model Ops/Applied ML teams to prepare a concise, technical-to-executive handoff that can be reviewed during a QBR or an ad-hoc postmortem review.

When to use this template

- Any sustained customer-facing degradation in automated evaluation metrics (examples: eval score drop >= 5% relative, BLEU/ROUGE delta, semantic-similarity regression, or embedding downstream accuracy drop).
- Significant rise in customer complaints tied to model outputs (false positives/negatives, hallucinations, policy violations).
- Persistent customer-side error-rate or latency increase that correlates with model changes.

Quick summary structure (one-slide / one-paragraph target)

1. Summary: what changed, when observed, customers impacted (count & priority).
2. Impact: short list of user-facing symptoms and metric deltas.
3. Immediate containment actions taken (if any).
4. Next steps & owners (72-hour action plan).

Stakeholders and ownership

- Customer Success (owner): primary customer liaison, collects customer evidence and priority, coordinates QBR agenda.
- Applied ML / Model Ops (owner): investigative lead on model changes, checkpoints, and rollback.
- Platform / Runtime (owner): verifies infra/serving factors (cache, routing, quantization variants, autoscaler).
- Solutions Engineering: provides reproduction harnesses or prompt sets.
- Legal / Security (as required): if regression leads to data exposure or policy violation.

Detection and verification checklist (first 60 minutes)

1. Confirm alert provenance: determine whether detection came from automated eval, telemetry, customer report, or test harness.
2. Reproduce with canonical prompt set: run the canonical prompt set used for eval and customer seeds. Capture diffs.
3. Verify rollout history: query model rollout timeline, pinned versions, and canary status.
   - Example: runbook query: SELECT version, rolled_at, rollout_type FROM model_rollouts WHERE model = 'text-sim-1' ORDER BY rolled_at DESC LIMIT 5;
4. Check serving variant parity: compare outputs across host, dedicated, and private variants (if customer on Dedicated/Private).
5. Confirm telemetry signals: inspect the following (examples):
   - Automated eval pipeline: mean_eval_score by day (last 14 days).
   - Production request sampling: failure_rate, latency_p50/p95, token_error_rate.
   - Output quality heuristics: hallucination_score, policy_violation_rate.
   - PromQL example: increase(error_count_total{job=\"inference\",customer_id=\"CUST-123\"}[30m]) / increase(requests_total{job=\"inference\",customer_id=\"CUST-123\"}[30m])

Immediate containment (hours 0–6)

- If regression confirmed and customer impact high: pin customer to previous model version or route to a verified fallback variant. Owner: Model Ops.
- Increase sampling: enable high-fidelity request capture for affected tenants for 72 hours (obfuscate PII per privacy policy). Owner: Platform + Customer Success.
- Rate-limit risky traffic patterns if outputs cause safety violations. Owner: Platform / Security.
- Notify affected customers (template below). Owner: Customer Success.

Sample customer notification (first touch)

Subject: Service update — investigation into observed output changes

Hi <Customer-Contact>,

We are investigating a change in model outputs that may affect your service. Our initial analysis shows a regression in automated quality metrics affecting approximately <X>% of recent requests. We have pinned your tenant to a known-good model version while our team investigates. We will share a detailed timeline and remediation plan within 24 hours.

If you have specific examples please reply to this thread or upload them to the shared bucket: s3://redwood-customer-evidence/<customer-id>

Regards,
Aisha Patel, Customer Success

Triage and root-cause analysis (6–48 hours)

1. Re-run controlled A/B: run affected model version vs previous pinned version on representative seed set. Capture token-level diffs and confidence/entropy metrics.
2. Check model artifacts: commit hashes, tokenizer versions, quantization steps, and any export-time flags.
3. Evaluate config drift: request batching size, KV cache warm-starts, truncation lengths, and tokenization truncation.
4. Review infra signals: kernel fallback events, out-of-memory metadata, preemption logs, and autoscale spikes.
5. Confirm no data/regression introduced via prompt templates or input sanitizers in the client stack.

Root cause classification matrix (use one)

| Root cause category | Typical indicators | Remediation pattern | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Model artifact regression | New model commit, metric drop in eval harness | Rollback to previous model; patch and re-run eval | Applied ML |
| Tokenizer/Preprocessing drift | Tokenization mismatch, different seq lengths | Re-align tokenizer, rebuild cache, re-evaluate | Model Ops |
| Serving variance (quantization/kernel) | Degraded samples only on quantized path | Serve from higher-precision variant; rebuild quant profile | Serving Runtime |
| Data-/training-distribution shift | Recent training data added, eval shift | Retrain with corrected dataset or mitigate via fine-tune | Research/Applied ML |
| Upstream prompt/contract change | New prompt templates causing output format change | Revert/normalize prompt, add validation at ingress | Solutions Eng/CS |

72-hour action plan template (deliverables and owners)

- Day 0–1: Containment (pin, sampling, customer comms) — Owner: Customer Success / Platform / Model Ops.
- Day 1–2: Diagnostic A/B, artifact review, infra check — Owner: Model Ops / Serving Runtime.
- Day 2–3: Fix candidate & test: either rollback or small patch + canary — Owner: Applied ML / Model Ops.
- Day 3: Customer validation & staged rollout plan — Owner: Customer Success / Solutions Eng.

QBR presentation structure (recommended slides)

1. Title slide: Incident/regression short summary.
2. Impact snapshot: customer(s) affected, user-visible symptoms, revenue/risk tier.
3. Telemetry timeline: eval-score, request volume, failure/latency, and sample outputs (before/after).
4. Root cause hypothesis & evidence.
5. Actions taken (containment & fixes) + status.
6. Risk & follow-up items (longer-term mitigations).
7. Acceptance criteria and rollback criteria for full rollout.

Metrics and thresholds to include in QBR

- Eval delta: relative drop in the chosen automated metric (e.g., mean_eval_score) — flag if >= 5% relative drop.
- Customer error reports: count and severity (P1/P2).
- Production mismatch rate: percentage of sampled requests where output differs meaningfully from canary baseline — flag if >= 4%.
- Latency and token error surge: p95 latency delta > 30% or token_error_rate > 0.5%.

Acceptance criteria for rollout back to production

- Automated eval shows improvement to within 1% of baseline across the canonical prompt set.
- Customer samples validated by Solutions Eng & CS (>= 50 representative samples).
- No recurring infra anomalies during 24-hour canary (no OOMs, kernel fallbacks).
- Observability enabled: alerts and synthetic checks for the next 14 days.

Follow-up prevention controls (long-term)

- Expand canary test harness to include customer-specific prompt sets for top-10 customers.
- Add preflight eval gating for quantized variants and tokenizer changes.
- Implement a ‘regression budget’ alert where cumulative delta across evals triggers a staged rollback.
- Strengthen QBR artifact template so every major model rollout includes an expected behavior doc and degradation scenarios.

Appendices

A. Example telemetry queries
- Eval trend (SQL): SELECT date_trunc('day', run_ts) AS day, avg(score) AS mean_eval_score FROM eval_runs WHERE model = 'prod-text-v2' AND seed_set = 'canonical' AND run_ts > now() - INTERVAL '14 days' GROUP BY day ORDER BY day;
- Sample diff (python snippet):
  ```python
  for seed in seeds:
      b = run_model(seed, version='prod-text-v2')
      a = run_model(seed, version='prod-text-v1')
      print(seed, compute_semantic_similarity(a, b))
  ```

B. Customer comms templates
- See the Sample customer notification above and the escalation email template in /confluence/customer-success-and-support/escalation-playbook/urgent-escalation-handoff-and-sla-triage-2026 for escalation variants.

D. Post-QBR follow-up cadence
- Within 1 week: publish short RCA with evidence bundles and action owners.
- Within 2–4 weeks: implement software hotfix or rollback and validate with customer.
- 30–90 days: incorporate preventative controls into release gating and QBR playbooks.

Document maintenance
- Owner: Customer Success (Aisha Patel).
- Review cadence: quarterly or after each major regression incident.
